units.translation: λισσὴ instead of ὁμαλή (smooth). But Amerias in his Glossai renders λισσόν as 'high'. That this island has birds that shoot with their feathers as with arrows is also recorded by Euripides in Phrixus (fr. 838 N.²).
b. 〈ἀπειρέσιοι:〉 many. Lg
c. ἐφέπουσιν: they pass time, they occupy themselves. Lg P
387a. Otirere and Antiope: these are queens of the Amazons.
b. 〈στρατόωντο: . . .〉 what army, no one has explained.

388-91a. For there for you: for there, on the island of Ares, an unspeakable benefit will come to you from the sea, clearly through the shipwreck. He means the sons of Phrixus and Chalciope, daughter of Aeetes, who, when they were sailing to Greece because of the inheritance of Athamas, were shipwrecked on this island and happened to receive care from the heroes and became guides for them to Scythia. These are Argus, Melas, Cytisorus, Phrontis.
b. 〈ἀδευκέος:〉 of the unexpected, instead of 'of the one appearing to you beyond hope'. Lm
c. He calls the sea ἀδευκῆ, that is, bitter; for δεῦκος means sweet. He calls the benefit unspeakable because of the unexpectedness of the shipwreck. P
d. τῷ κέ τε φίλα φρο〈νέων〉: therefore, since he will benefit you, being well-disposed to you I bid you to hold back.

e. 〈ἀλλὰ τίη με:〉 he says this because he did not notice that he was about to say everything—who the people they would meet were and what they would do for them—and to go beyond what had been foretold to him; for he had said
for (v. 311 sqq.) that he would not say everything precisely, so as not to offend the gods again. Therefore he checks himself.
f. 〈ἀλιτέσϑαι:〉 to err. Lg
g. 〈διηνεκέως:〉 throughout, in general. Lg

392-94a. But beyond the island: after the island and the opposite mainland dwell the Philyres. Above the Philyres and in front are the Macrones, a Scythian tribe or a colony of the Euboeans; for Euboea was also called Macris because of its position.

b. But beyond the island: in front of the island of Ares and of the land opposite dwell the Philyres, who were named after Philyra, daughter of Oceanus, wife of Cronus, and mother of Chiron, who spent time there. Or thus: after the island and the opposite mainland the Philyres dwell.
c. περιώσια: many. He says this because they are scattered over a large territory.
d. 〈φῦλα Βεχείρων κτλ.:〉 Scythian tribes. Lg P
395. Next the Sapeires after them: after the Becheires. The Sapeires are a Scythian tribe so named because the sapphire stone is found in abundance among them.
396a. 〈Βύζηρες:〉 a Scythian tribe. Lg
b. ὁμώλακες: neighbors. For ὤλαξ is the Doric form of αὖλαξ (furrow); and Homer (N 707) 'ἱεμένω κατὰ ὦλκα'.
397-98a. ἀρήιοι: either those warlike by nature or those dear and sacred to Ares. Lm (P)
